body.input: Which companies expanded to Norway in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, here are notable companies that expanded to or within Norway in 2026:

## Logistics & Services
- **Crane Worldwide Logistics** — Opened a new office in **Stavanger, Norway** in September 2026 as part of a broader Nordic expansion (also opening in Copenhagen and Gothenburg). The move was aimed at supporting customers in industries such as renewable energy, advanced manufacturing, and life sciences.

- **Gray Dawes Group** — The UK-based travel management company expanded its Nordic reach by forming a strategic partnership with Norway's **Berg-Hansen**, strengthening its ability to serve international clients in the Norwegian market.

## Energy & Data Centers
- **Bitzero Holdings** (NASDAQ: AIBZ) — Expanded its data center facility in **Namsskogan, Norway**, receiving key transformers to grow capacity from 40 MW to 110 MW. Construction firm **Skanska** and power/cooling specialist **Vertiv** are engaged on site.

- **SLB** (formerly Schlumberger) — Selected by Vår Energi in November 2026 as its main integrated drilling services supplier for two offshore rigs on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, expanding its operational role in Norway through a four-year contract (with options to extend through 2034).

## Oil & Gas Exploration (APA 2026 Licensing Round)
Twenty-one E&P companies applied for Norway's APA 2026 offshore exploration licensing round (announced May 5, 2026), which expanded the predefined area by 70 blocks across the North Sea, Norwegian Sea, and Barents Sea. The full list of applicants includes:

1. A/S Norske Shell
2. Aker BP
3. Concedo
4. ConocoPhillips Skandinavia
5. DNO Norge
6. Equinor Energy
7. Harbour Energy Norge
8. INPEX Idemitsu Norge
9. Japex Norge
10. Kistos Energy Norway
11. Lime Petroleum
12. OKEA
13. OMV Norge
14. ORLEN Upstream Norway
15. Pandion Energy
16. Petrolia NOCO
17. Repsol Norge
18. Source Energy
19. TotalEnergies EP Norge
20. Vår Energi
21. Wellesley Petroleum

License awards are expected in early 2027.

## Notable Exit
- **Johnson & Johnson** announced it is pulling its pharmaceutical operations from Norway, moving in the opposite direction.

---

*Note: Norway's data center sector saw significant expansion interest in 2026, prompting the government to freeze new grid capacity reservations on November 9, 2026 and announce a forthcoming licensing scheme to manage demand (applications for ~26,000 MW of new consumption were filed, with data centers accounting for three-quarters of that total).*

Strategically located in three of the region's leading commercial and logistics hubs, the new offices provide customers with access to local expertise backed by Crane Worldwide Logistics' global network and technology-driven supply chain solutions. The Nordic region continues to play a significant role in international trade, advanced manufacturing, life sciences, technology, renewable energy and industrial production. Dave Bishop, Chief Operating Officer at Gray Dawes Group, said the partnership was intended to strengthen the company’s ability to support clients in key markets rather than simply expand its international footprint.

“Delivering a genuinely global travel management proposition means having the right people, expertise and service capabilities in the markets that matter to our clients,” he said.

“Berg-Hansen has an established reputation, deep local knowledge and a service-led approach that aligns closely with our own. By combining their Nordic expertise with our own international operations and existing partner relationships, we can offer clients greater geographical reach while maintaining the quality of service they expect from Gray Dawes.” [...] Bishop also suggested the partnership reflects wider changes taking place within the industry following the acquisition of CWT by American Express Global Business Travel.

“We also see an opportunity to bring together other TMCs that may be reassessing their international partnerships as a result of the ongoing consolidation in our industry,” he said.

Suzanne Horner, Chief Executive Officer of Gray Dawes Group, said the deal reflected growing demand from clients for international support without sacrificing local expertise and personal service. [...] Petter Brodahl, Executive Vice President, Partner Relations at Berg-Hansen, said: “Our partnership with Gray Dawes gives our clients access to an established international travel management company that shares our commitment to personal service and quality.”

Gunnar Gunnarsen, Executive Vice President, Sales and Business Development at Berg-Hansen, added: “International companies need the best of both worlds: flexibility and strong local expertise, combined with technology and a global platform for data and insights. This partnership brings those strengths together, enabling us to serve customers consistently across markets.”

# Press Release

## SLB Selected by Vår Energi for Integrated Drilling Services Offshore Norway

12 November 2026

PDF Version 167 KB

Four-year scope covers two offshore rigs on the Norwegian Continental Shelf

HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 12, 2026-- Global energy technology company SLB (NYSE: SLB) today announced it has been selected by Vår Energi as its main integrated drilling services supplier for the Transocean Barents and Deepsea Bergen rigs on the Norwegian Continental Shelf.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: [...] Key Points:

 SLB has been selected by Vår Energi as its main integrated drilling services supplier for two offshore rigs on the Norwegian Continental Shelf.
 The initial four-year scope includes four one-year extension options that could extend the work through 2034.
 The selection expands SLB’s relationship with Vår Energi across drilling, digital well and field development planning, and subsea production systems.

About SLB [...] The integrated delivery model brings together technical expertise, digital workflows and operational execution across the well delivery process. Working closely with Vår Energi and other selected service and technology providers, SLB will connect planning and execution, simplify interfaces, and use data to support faster decisions and more consistent well performance.

The selection also expands SLB’s role in Vår Energi’s offshore operations, adding integrated drilling services to an established relationship spanning digital well and field development planning and subsea production systems through SLB’s OneSubsea™ joint venture.

## Licensing Will Cover New and Existing Sites

Digitalization Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said the licensing scheme should be ready in autumn 2027 and will apply to existing data centers as well as new ones, with transition terms to be worked out with industry. He cited health, defense, mobile networks and artificial intelligence as beneficial uses. Cryptocurrency mining will not qualify. Energy Minister Terje Aasland said Statnett has received applications for about 26,000 MW of new consumption this year. Data centers account for three-quarters of that total.

The government also wants large new consumers to pay more toward grid and system operating costs. It plans talks with industry on new generation such as offshore wind and gas power with carbon capture and storage. [...] Environment+Energy Leader logo

# Norway Halts New Grid Reservations for Server Facilities

## Statnett has frozen new grid reservations for data centers until as late as Aug. 1, 2027, while the government drafts a licensing scheme that will rank which facilities Norway wants.

420 kV Reisadalen – Skillemoen power line, Norway [...] 420 kV Reisadalen – Skillemoen power line, Norway

Statnett, Norway's transmission system operator, stopped accepting new grid capacity reservations from data centers on Nov. 9. It also paused work on some of the technical approvals that projects need before they can energize. The same day, the government moved to announce a licensing scheme that will decide which data centers the country wants. Statnett's figures show 800 megawatts (MW) of data center load connected, 4,200 MW reserved, 9,100 MW in the queue and inquiries for another 18,000 MW. Norway's peak demand is just over 25,000 MW.
